prompt_en: A cinematic documentary photograph of an inhabited territorial estate whose resources are administered with its resident community. At a village bakehouse opening, the reference-guided woman and the estate's residents take part in a public exchange about a shared estate resource. Use the supplied image as the face and hair appearance reference for the woman: preserve her softly oval face, large dark brown eyes, natural nose and lips, and short dark bob with fine separated bangs. Her attentive presence and quiet, almost amused smile give the scene a subtle human warmth. The woman stands beside a long waist-high bread table outside the stone bakehouse, wearing a fitted forest-green wool jacket with a small brass estate seal at its collar and a softly draped ivory shirt. She has just received a warm round loaf from the working baker and is presenting it back to him to break for the waiting residents. Both of her hands support the near half of the loaf from beneath; the baker's flour-dusted hands support its far half across the table. Their forearms lead visibly to their separate bodies. They look at each other as he begins to pull the crust apart, revealing a small bright tear in the loaf between them. Beside the exchange, a clerk checks an open ruled register on the near end of the table beside two distinct wooden grain bins. The first bin is open and contains visible loose grain; the other bin beside it is separately closed by its own fitted wooden lid. The clerk looks down at the register and points along one line with a free forefinger while a resident places a small wooden tally beside the book. Both bin tops, the exposed grain, the complete closed lid, the clerk and the record remain visible together. The nearby waiting people attend to the tally-and-register exchange. Behind the baker, the bakehouse doorway reveals the red mouth of a working masonry oven and loaded bread racks. Fresh pale mortar around the oven arch contrasts with smoke-darkened older stone. A modest cloth pennant carries the same brass-colored seal as the woman's collar. Village roofs and cultivated plots descend behind the square toward the estate's distant manor. The table cuts diagonally through a medium-wide landscape frame, the woman's face, the shared loaf, the register and the residents' response remaining readable together. Soft late-afternoon daylight enters from the open square, meeting the warm oven glow. Natural skin and flour textures, restrained earth colors, a 40 mm documentary perspective and enough depth of field to connect this intimate exchange to the working place.
